title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: Elemental metals Cr, Fe, V, W and either Ta or Ti powders/ingots
recollection.intervention: CALPHAD and first-principles calculations of phase stability followed by experimental arc-melting and heat-treatment of equiatomic CrFeVWTa and CrFeVWTi alloys
recollection.structure: Predominantly single BCC solid-solution for the Ta-containing alloy, and a BCC matrix plus a σ-type intermetallic for the Ti-containing alloy
recollection.mechanism: High configurational entropy favors the BCC solid-solution; differences in atomic size and enthalpy of mixing drive σ-phase formation when Ti is used
recollection.results: Theory predicted ΔGmix < –10 kJ mol⁻¹ and a stability window up to ~1200 °C for the Ta alloy, matching XRD/SEM observations of a single BCC phase with lattice parameter ≈ 2.93 Å; Vickers hardness ~600 HV. The Ti alloy showed calculated miscibility gaps below 1000 °C, experimentally confirmed by ~15 vol % σ-phase after annealing, with hardness ~520 HV.

score.note: The recollection substantially misidentifies the study. It replaces the actual MD/hybrid MD–MC, mechanical-alloying, SPS, and thermal-diffusivity work with CALPHAD/DFT and arc melting. It also reverses or invents phase findings: the Ta alloy actually formed a bcc matrix plus Fe2Ta C14 Laves phase, while the Ti alloy had two bcc-type phases rather than a σ phase. The proposed Ti-driven σ-phase mechanism is therefore wrong. Reported energies, temperatures, phase fractions, lattice parameter, and hardness are unsupported; the actual quantitative results include lattice parameters near 3.12 Å and 3.10/2.98 Å, >98% density, and thermal diffusivity of about 3.5–7 mm²/s.
